practicalQuestion: How should we structure training between two competitions inside 96 hours?

decisionContext.outcome: Preserve readiness without losing tactical preparation
decisionContext.constraints: Travel after the first competition; one field session available

evidenceConfidence.rationale: One directly relevant systematic review addresses congested competition, while the supporting recovery review is broader and group-level evidence does not resolve individual response.

dimensions.directness: One congestion review; one broader recovery review
dimensions.consistency: Aligned on caution; no universal dose rule
dimensions.transferability: Professional and elite cohorts, not Baylor-specific

bottomLine.text: Use a recovery-priority between-match plan. Pooled total distance may be preserved, but broader physical effects remain inconsistent and group summaries do not establish individual recovery.

recommendedDirection.text: Remove nonessential load, preserve only the preparation needed for the next competition, and individualize from multiple within-athlete signals rather than total distance or one group marker.

actions.title: Separate exposure groups
actions.text: Separate high-minute, low-minute, and returning athletes before assigning recovery, maintenance, or top-up work.

actions.title: Remove nonessential load
actions.text: Keep the field exposure focused enough to remove nonessential between-match load.

monitoring.label: Readiness
monitoring.text: Interpret recent exposure, athlete report, symptoms, and a stable within-athlete performance measure together.

guardrails.text: Maintained total distance does not establish complete recovery.
Do not let a group biomarker result operate as an individual readiness diagnosis.

limitations.text: The direct congestion review is concentrated in professional male soccer, limiting transferability to other collegiate populations.

whatCouldChange.text: Direct collegiate, female-athlete, or sport-specific evidence could change the direction or confidence.

evidenceTension.text: Pooled total distance was not reduced, while the broader review described physical-performance effects as equivocal.

sources.sourceFile: The effect of fixture congestion on performance during professional male soccer match play - A systematic critical review with meta-analysis.pdf
sources.citation: Julian R, Page RM, Harper LD. The effect of fixture congestion on performance during professional male soccer match-play: A systematic critical review with meta-analysis. Sports Medicine. 2021;51(2):255-273.

sources.sourceFile: Acute effects of training loads on muscle damage markers and performance in semi-elite and elite athletes - A systematic review and meta-analysis.pdf
sources.citation: Simmons R, Doma K, Sinclair W, Connor J, Leicht A. Acute effects of training loads on muscle damage markers and performance in semi-elite and elite athletes: A systematic review and meta-analysis. Sports Medicine. 2021;51(10):2181-2207.

claims.text: Fixture congestion did not affect pooled total distance covered.

evidence.excerpt: Fixture congestion had no impact on total distance covered

claims.text: The review described the effects on physical performance as equivocal.

evidence.excerpt: fixture congestion has equivocal effects on physical performance

claims.text: The group-level recovery review did not identify within-athlete or position-specific differences across time.

evidence.excerpt: The group level meta-analysis failed to identify within-athlete or position-specific differences across time.
